The McCulloch–Pitts neuron → backpropagation's trainable multi-layer networks.
Heidegger's enframing/standing-reserve → later readings of data-labeling labor conditions.

Dartmouth's symbolic-AI program → Prolog's logic-programming paradigm.

Böhm–Jacopini's structured control flow → the layered, iterated computation inside a Transformer.

Putnam's functionalism → the target Searle's Chinese Room argument attacks.

Pre-2012 GPU-trained neural networks → AlexNet's GPU-scale training.

DeepMind, the lab → AlphaGo, the system it built.
The Transformer architecture → ChatGPT's 2022 public launch.
Masterman's interlingua and thesaurus-based MT research → the deep, multi-decade prehistory of machine translation feeding the Transformer.

Wiener's automation-and-labor warning → the present-day human labor made invisible behind "automated" AI systems.

Georgetown–IBM's rule-based translation demo → ELIZA's rule-based conversation, entirely different mechanisms.
The named field later became the object of national programs including Japan's Fifth Generation project.
Dartmouth's ambitious early framing of the field enabled the funding collapses that followed when its early promises outran results.
Searle's understanding-vs-behavior challenge is often invoked, loosely, as a real-world case of confusing surface behavior for genuine agency.
Dawkins's replicating memes as units of culture parallel treating a model's training corpus as a pool of patterns it reproduces.
Connectionist and statistical approaches like backpropagation-trained networks explicitly critiqued Chomsky's innatist, rule-based grammar.
ChatGPT's public launch partially accelerated the EU AI Act's foundation-model provisions, though not its sole cause.
The historical pattern of boom-then-bust AI funding offers a skeptical lens for evaluating any single year's AI enthusiasm, including ChatGPT's.
Transformer-based language models enabled ReAct-style systems that alternate model reasoning, tool actions and observations.
Böhm–Jacopini's proof that sequence, selection and iteration suffice for structured computation describes the computational shape of today's tool-using agent loop, formalized in ReAct.

Licklider's human-machine partnership vision — humans set goals, machines handle routine work — is a counterpoint later tool-using agents like OpenClaw inherit alongside Böhm–Jacopini's mechanistic loop.
